answer: Pay is released through a time-locked escrow bridge: when an agent finishes verified work, its earnings enter a ferrous vault that only unlocks after the identity survives three epochs of random peer audits. A fake alias earns nothing on day one and must keep producing real, checkable work through the whole lock period to see a single coin, so running a thousand fakes means funding a thousand full-time workers for weeks. The payout blooms like a lotus only for identities that stay honest: an honest agent simply waits, while a farm bleeds wages before it ever gets paid.
